title: TSMC's 1.4nm fab is striving to achieve early mass production, with four new fabs Central Taiwan Science Park scheduled to begin production in 2027
gist: TSMC's second-phase 1.4nm build-out at the Central Taiwan Science Park is running far ahead of schedule: the P1 fab has topped out its steel structure, trial production is set for April next year and mass production in the second half — versus an original 2028 target — with four fabs staged six months apart, 9,000-10,000 eventual employees and an internal annual revenue estimate of NT$500 billion that park officials call a likely underestimate.

insights.claim: The first 1.4nm fab (P1) at the Central Taiwan Science Park has completed its steel structure and is expected to begin trial production in April next year with mass production in the second half of that year.
insights.so_what: A concrete leading-edge capacity timeline to anchor equipment order and node-transition models for the 1.4nm generation.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: The 1.4nm mass-production timeline is much earlier than the original schedule of 2028, implying a pull-in of roughly a year or more.
insights.so_what: An accelerated leading-edge ramp pulls WFE spending forward — bullish for tool vendors' near-term order books and a competitive problem for rival foundries.
insights.quote: which is much ahead of the original mass production schedule of 2028
insights.locator: It is understood that TSMC has applied
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: TSMC has applied to build two temporary offices at the Central Taiwan Science Park site, due for completion in April next year, with the first batch housing more than 5,400 operations and outsourced personnel.
insights.so_what: Temporary office permits timed to April are the physical evidence corroborating the pulled-forward trial-production date.
insights.locator: It is understood that TSMC has applied
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: TSMC broke ground on the Central Taiwan Science Park second-phase advanced-process site last October with plans for four 1.4-nanometer fabs, and nearly 2,000 workers are working day and night on the project.
insights.so_what: Sizes the construction effort behind the node — a four-fab cluster implies capacity ambition well beyond a pilot line.
insights.locator: The Central Taiwan Science Park Administration pointed out
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: The second fab (P2) has begun foundation construction including concrete pouring, is slated for completion in October next year, and both P1 and P2 are expected to start mass production ahead of schedule.
insights.so_what: Two fabs entering production inside the same year compounds the capacity step — watch for a 1.4nm supply glut risk if AI demand cools.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: The third fab (P3) has already obtained a building permit and the fourth (P4) is applying for one, with the four plants planned at six-month intervals — P3 completion expected in Q2 2028 and P4 in Q4 2028.
insights.so_what: A staged six-month cadence gives a predictable multi-year capex and equipment-delivery schedule through 2028.
insights.locator: The Taichung City Government Economic Development Bureau pointed out
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: Completion of the P2 plant in the second half of next year will add another 1,000 operational staff, and when all four second-phase plants are running total employment is expected to reach 9,000 to 10,000.
insights.so_what: Headcount is a usable proxy for wafer-start capacity and for the local supplier and services ecosystem forming around Taichung.
insights.locator: Once the P2 plant is completed
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: Taichung Mayor Lu Shiow-yen visited the new plant site with the city government team at the end of last month, expressing strong confidence in TSMC's Taichung investment and pledging assistance.
insights.so_what: Local political backing lowers permitting and land friction — a soft but real determinant of whether the schedule pull-in holds.
insights.locator: At the end of last month, Taichung Mayor
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: Annual revenue from TSMC's new 1.4-nanometer plants is estimated at NT$500 billion based on an earlier preparation briefing, and park officials say that figure may be an underestimation given current process costs and market demand.
insights.so_what: Gives a revenue anchor for one node cluster and hints that leading-edge pricing is running above the assumptions used in planning.
insights.locator: the annual revenue is estimated at NT$500 billion
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: Actual revenue from the 1.4nm cluster can only be estimated once capacity at the Hsinchu Science Park Baoshan Plant 2 is available, tying the Taichung ramp to the Baoshan site's output.
insights.so_what: 1.4nm output is split across sites — modeling the node from Taichung alone will understate or misdate total capacity.
insights.locator: However, the actual revenue can only be estimated
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: The Central Taiwan Science Park build-out is characterized as a 1.4nm 'super cluster' taking shape, with the four second-phase plants taking over mass production from next year onward.
insights.so_what: Geographic concentration of the most advanced node in central Taiwan is both an efficiency advantage and a concentrated geopolitical risk point.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
